mu_name_from: MuMain loads boot indexes 10 to 14 from BootElf{i+1} (ZzzOpenData.cpp line 152: `AccessModel(MODEL_BOOTS + i + 10, ..., L"BootElf", i + 1)`), so index 13 is BootElf04, which openmu's 0.75 Armors.cs names the Spirit Boots. mu.db agrees: code 5645, group 11 index 13, Player/BootElf04.bmd.
why_this_one: The Fairy Elf's fourth set and the first of her two that are plate: Eo the Craftsman sells all five pieces at +3 on the first row of his shelf (src/sim/market.cpp, kCraftsman), so Noria's second merchant had a shelf whose top half could not be looked at. Spirit is the Brass set's metal in the elf's green: the same 10-series sheets MU recoloured with a `c`.
profile_from: armour, not soft_armour. Vine, Silk and Wind are hide and cloth and took soft_armour; Spirit is plate. Its sheets are the Brass set's 10-series in the elf's green - upper_10c and lower_10c are upper_10_m and lower_10_m repainted, and the Brass set is plate_steel with brass ornaments - so the default plate_steel is what most of it is, and the `c` recolour changes the paint and not how the thing was made.

stats.note: The item's own row, copied from OpenMU's 0.75 initialiser rather than restated, with the call it came from beside it.
stats.from: openmu/src/Persistence/Initialization/Version075/Items/Armors.cs line 134. The 0.75 table, which is the version this server is being built to.
stats.call_note: ArmorInitializerBase.CreateBoots(number, slot, width, height, name, dropLevel, defense, walkSpeed, durability, strengthRequirement, agilityRequirement, darkWizardClassLevel, darkKnightClassLevel, elfClassLevel). Slot 6, so the group is 11.
stats.defense_note: Points of defence, in the row and summed into Player.ArmourDefense by Wear - see shared/Rows.cs.
stats.walk_speed_note: Nought, as on every elf boot: the row's own asymmetry against the knight's, recorded rather than smoothed.
stats.classes_from: The last three ints of the call are 0, 0, 1 - the Fairy Elf alone. Eighty agility beside forty strength is the row saying the same thing in stats.

sheet_from: Data/Player/boot_10c.OZJ (64x64), lower_09c.OZT (32x32) and boots_10.OZJ (64x64), from MuMain. The .bmd names boot_10c.jpg, lower_09c.tga and boots_10.jpg; 130 of the 142 triangles are on the first, 4 on lower_09c and 8 on boots_10. boots_10.png was already in the tree, decoded for the Brass Boots, and is reused.
sheet_note: boot_10c is the boot from two sides, green greaves with gold ribbing and a gold-studded cuff, mean (59, 91, 72) at chroma 53. boots_10 is the Brass Boots' own gold sheet, unrecoloured: MU left eight triangles of the knight's gold on the elf's boot. lower_09c is the curled green-and-gold fin on two crossed quads.
material_note: Six islands, and the counts are the Brass Boots' own - 53, 53, 16, 16, 2, 2 - which is how you know it is the same mesh repainted. Islands 0 and 1 are the two greaves, boot_10c's; islands 2 and 3 are the cuffs, boot_10c's 12 and boots_10's 4 each - the gold the Brass Boots wear, left unrecoloured on the cuff. All four plate_steel. Islands 4 and 5 are two triangles each, lower_09c's 4: the curled fins on crossed quads standing off the calf where the Brass Boots have boots_10b's gold fan, brass as those are. The green is dark - lower_10c averages lum about 60 - and a dark albedo at metallic 1.0 is the shape of the Bone set's fault, so it was weighed: here it is plate, as the Bronze-green Scale set's verdigris plate is (HelmMale07's note), and the gold ribbing is what the metal's highlight has to catch.
